class="docs-prompt-preview" aria-label="Prompt preview" tabindex="0">You&#x27;re Claude Code, working in my repository.

Task
Make the page&#x27;s `/loop 10m /run-tests` example work in this repository: create a project skill at .agents/skills/run-tests/SKILL.md that runs this repo&#x27;s test command, summarizes failures in a few lines and changes nothing. Then add docs/muse-session.md for the team with the commands that matter here: /goal for long tasks, /loop with this skill, /compact and /recap, /fork and /rewind, /stop versus Esc, and the steering keys.

Read this first
Meta&#x27;s docs page &quot;Working with the agent&quot; as Markdown: https://dev.meta.ai/docs/muse-code/interactive.md
It&#x27;s the source of truth for request and response shapes. The same page for people: https://dev.meta.ai/docs/muse-code/interactive

Setup
- Muse Code: muse on PATH (install: curl -fsSL https://dev.meta.ai/install.sh | sh, or irm https://dev.meta.ai/install.ps1 | iex on Windows; check: muse --version). Its default model is muse-spark-1.2; --model picks another.
- Auth: muse reads META_API_KEY from the environment (in CI, from the secret store), else a key stored with muse auth set or a browser sign-in; not MODEL_API_KEY. Never hard-code, print or commit the key.
- Python: a plain script that runs muse through subprocess where a step needs it.

Facts to get right
- /loop takes an interval (5m, 1h, 2d) or a quoted 5-field cron in local time; no cadence means every 10 minutes. Jobs expire after 7 days; an occurrence during an active run is skipped.
- Project skills live at &lt;repo&gt;/.agents/skills/&lt;skill-id&gt;/SKILL.md (name and description front matter, as Claude Code and Codex skills use). Check one with `muse skills validate &lt;dir&gt;`.
- While a turn runs: Enter steers it, Alt+Enter queues for the next turn, Esc interrupts it (not background work: that&#x27;s /stop), Esc on an empty composer retracts the newest queued item.
- /compact summarizes context (lossy for the model; scrollback stays); /recap summarizes recent activity without changing context.
- /new keeps scrollback, /clear wipes it; /fork branches from the latest point; /rewind from an earlier message; /side opens a side conversation.

Starter code (Python)
import pathlib
import subprocess

skill = pathlib.Path(&quot;.agents/skills/run-tests/SKILL.md&quot;)
skill.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
skill.write_text(&quot;&quot;&quot;---
name: run-tests
description: Run this repo&#x27;s test suite and summarize failures. Used by /loop 10m /run-tests.
---
# Run the tests

1. Run the test command from the repo root (use this repo&#x27;s real one).
2. Report the pass and fail counts, then each failure in one line with its file.
3. Change nothing: no edits, no commits.
&quot;&quot;&quot;)
subprocess.run([&quot;muse&quot;, &quot;skills&quot;, &quot;validate&quot;, str(skill.parent)], check=True)

Done when
- `muse skills validate ./.agents/skills/run-tests` passes, and the skill uses this repo&#x27;s real test command.
- docs/muse-session.md lists /loop 10m /run-tests and each other command with one line on when to use it.
- The key comes from META_API_KEY or a stored sign-in and never appears in code, logs or commits.</pre><div class="docs-prompt-foot"><span class="docs-prompt-count">3,028<!-- --> fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.6" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" aria-hidden="true" focusable="false"><path d="M6 9.5l6 6 6-6"></path></svg></button><div id="_R_95av5spfklb_" class="docs-toc-panel" hidden=""></div></nav></div><p class="docs-p">The interactive session is where you drive Muse Code. Run <code class="docs-code-inline">muse</code> in a project and you get a terminal UI: type a prompt to start a turn, watch the agent work, and steer it with <strong>slash commands</strong>. This page covers the commands and shortcuts you use most.</p><p class="docs-p">To run one prompt to completion without a UI, see <a class="docs-link" href="/docs/muse-code/extending#headless">headless and CI</a>.</p><h2 id="slash-commands" class="docs-h docs-h2">Slash commands<a class="docs-anchor" href="#slash-commands" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1">#</a></h2><p class="docs-p">Type <code class="docs-code-inline">/</code> in the composer to open the command palette. Keep typing to filter. Every command on this page is built in; run <code class="docs-code-inline">/help</code> to see the full set in your workspace, and <code class="docs-code-inline">/keymap</code> for keyboard shortcuts.</p><p class="docs-p">A command is either <strong>safe to run mid-turn</strong> or <strong>held until the turn ends</strong>. The UI tells you which when a run is active. A few commands are unavailable inside a <a class="docs-link" href="/docs/muse-code/interactive#side-chats">side conversation</a>, and say so when you try them.</p><h2 id="steering" class="docs-h docs-h2">Steer a running turn<a class="docs-anchor" href="#steering" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1">#</a></h2><p class="docs-p">You don&#x27;t have to wait for the agent to finish. While a turn is running:</p><ul class="docs-list"><li><span><strong><code class="docs-code-inline">Enter</code> (steer)</strong>: submit text to <em>inject into the turn in progress</em>. The agent applies it on its next step.</span></li><li><span><strong><code class="docs-code-inline">Alt+Enter</code> (queue)</strong>: hold your text for the <em>next</em> turn instead of the current one.</span></li><li><span><strong><code class="docs-code-inline">Esc</code> (interrupt)</strong>: cancel the current turn. <code class="docs-code-inline">Esc</code> stops the turn only. It does <strong>not</strong> stop <a class="docs-link" href="/docs/muse-code/interactive#stop">background terminals</a> or subagents.</span></li><li><span><strong><code class="docs-code-inline">Esc</code> on an empty composer (retract)</strong>: pull the most recently queued instruction back into the composer to edit or drop it. Repeat to retract older ones. Only the newest eligible item is retractable at a time.</span></li></ul><p class="docs-p"><code class="docs-code-inline">Ctrl+C</code> also interrupts, but only from an empty composer. With text in the composer, it clears the input instead.</p><div class="docs-callout docs-callout-note" role="note"><span class="docs-callout-icon"><svg width="20" height="20" viewBox="0 0 20 20" aria-hidden="true" focusable="false"><circle cx="10" cy="10" r="8.5" fill="currentColor"></circle><path fill="#fff" d="M9.1 8.6h1.8v5.6H9.1z M10 5.3a1.1 1.1 0 1 1 0 2.2 1.1 1.1 0 0 1 0-2.2z"></path></svg></span><div class="docs-callout-body"><p class="docs-callout-title">Esc and /stop differ</p><p class="docs-p">If you interrupt a turn while background work is still running, Muse Code sets a reminder to run <a class="docs-link" href="/docs/muse-code/interactive#stop"><code class="docs-code-inline">/stop</code></a>. These are two separate actions: <code class="docs-code-inline">Esc</code> interrupts the turn, and <code class="docs-code-inline">/stop</code> stops background processes.</p></div></div><h2 id="sessions" class="docs-h docs-h2">Manage the session<a class="docs-anchor" href="#sessions" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1">#</a></h2><p class="docs-p">Each run is an append-only event log (see <a class="docs-link" href="/docs/muse-code/interactive#session-model">how sessions work</a>). These commands start, switch, and branch sessions:</p><div class="docs-code"><div class="docs-code-head"><span class="docs-code-label">text</span><span class="docs-code-tools"><button type="button" class="docs-copy-btn" aria-label="Copy code" title="Copy code"><svg width="16" height="16" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.6" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" aria-hidden="true" focusable="false"><path d="M9 9h10.5v10.5H9z M15 9V5.5A1.5 1.5 0 0 0 13.5 4h-8A1.5 1.5 0 0 0 4 5.5v8A1.5 1.5 0 0 0 5.5 15H9"></path></svg><span class="sr-only" aria-live="polite"></span></button></span></div><div role="group" aria-label="text" class="docs-code-body"><pre class="shiki docs" tabindex="0"><code><span class="line">/new       # start a fresh session, keep the terminal scrollback</span>
<span class="line">/clear     # start a fresh session and wipe the scrollback</span>
<span class="line">/name      # show or rename this session</span>
<span class="line">/resume    # pick a retained session to resume (this workspace)</span>
<span class="line">/resume --last   # resume the most recent session in this workspace</span>
<span class="line">/fork      # branch a new session from the current point</span></code></pre></div></div><ul class="docs-list"><li><span><strong><code class="docs-code-inline">/new</code> vs <code class="docs-code-inline">/clear</code></strong>: both begin a new session. The conversation, in-session context, token counts, goal, and tasks all reset. The only difference is your terminal scrollback: <code class="docs-code-inline">/new</code> keeps it on screen, and <code class="docs-code-inline">/clear</code> clears it. Neither changes on-disk <a class="docs-link" href="/docs/muse-code/configuration#local-memory">memory or rules</a>.</span></li><li><span><strong><code class="docs-code-inline">/name</code></strong>: shows the current session name or assigns one with <code class="docs-code-inline">/name &lt;name&gt;</code>. A stable name lets other live sessions find this one through <a class="docs-link" href="/docs/muse-code/session-messaging">session messaging</a>.</span></li><li><span><strong><code class="docs-code-inline">/resume</code></strong>: reopens a retained session and continues it. Resume is scoped to the current workspace and relaunches the session rather than swapping it in place, so expect a brief transition.</span></li><li><span><strong><code class="docs-code-inline">/fork</code></strong>: branches a <em>new</em> session from the current session&#x27;s latest stable point. The source session stays active and unchanged, and the fork doesn&#x27;t take over your view. Continue the fork later with <code class="docs-code-inline">muse resume &lt;fork-id&gt;</code>.</span></li></ul><p class="docs-p">To branch from an earlier user message, run <code class="docs-code-inline">/rewind</code> or press <code class="docs-code-inline">Esc</code> twice from an idle, empty composer. See <a class="docs-link" href="/docs/muse-code/rewind">rewind a conversation</a>. Rewind restores the selected message as an unsent draft in a new retained session and leaves workspace files unchanged.</p><p class="docs-p">To keep independent sessions active at the same time, start Muse Code in separate terminals. See <a class="docs-link" href="/docs/muse-code/session-messaging#parallel-sessions">run sessions in parallel</a> for workspace and worktree guidance.</p><h2 id="side-chats" class="docs-h docs-h2">Side conversations<a class="docs-anchor" href="#side-chats" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1">#</a></h2><p class="docs-p">Start a short parallel conversation without a change to the main thread:</p><div class="docs-code"><div class="docs-code-head"><span class="docs-code-label">text</span><span class="docs-code-tools"><button type="button" class="docs-copy-btn" aria-label="Copy code" title="Copy code"><svg width="16" height="16" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.6" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" aria-hidden="true" focusable="false"><path d="M9 9h10.5v10.5H9z M15 9V5.5A1.5 1.5 0 0 0 13.5 4h-8A1.5 1.5 0 0 0 4 5.5v8A1.5 1.5 0 0 0 5.5 15H9"></path></svg><span class="sr-only" aria-live="polite"></span></button></span></div><div role="group" aria-label="text" class="docs-code-body"><pre class="shiki docs" tabindex="0"><code><span class="line">/side              # open a side conversation</span>
<span class="line">/side &lt;prompt&gt;     # open one and send the first message</span>
<span class="line">/btw &lt;prompt&gt;      # alias for /side</span></code></pre></div></div><p class="docs-p">Muse Code seeds a side conversation from the main session&#x27;s history, but runs it as its own thread. It snapshots your main transcript and any in-flight run, and sets them aside. Press <code class="docs-code-inline">Ctrl+C</code> to return to the main thread. Muse Code restores it exactly, including a run that finished while you were away.</p><p class="docs-p">You can have one side conversation open at a time. While you&#x27;re in it, <code class="docs-code-inline">/side</code>, <code class="docs-code-inline">/fork</code>, <code class="docs-code-inline">/new</code>, <code class="docs-code-inline">/clear</code>, and <code class="docs-code-inline">/resume</code> are unavailable. Return to the main chat first. <code class="docs-code-inline">/copy</code> works and copies the side transcript.</p><h2 id="context" class="docs-h docs-h2">Control the context<a class="docs-anchor" href="#context" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1">#</a></h2><p class="docs-p">These commands manage what the model sees and let you save what it produced:</p><div class="docs-code"><div class="docs-code-head"><span class="docs-code-label">text</span><span class="docs-code-tools"><button type="button" class="docs-copy-btn" aria-label="Copy code" title="Copy code"><svg width="16" height="16" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.6" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" aria-hidden="true" focusable="false"><path d="M9 9h10.5v10.5H9z M15 9V5.5A1.5 1.5 0 0 0 13.5 4h-8A1.5 1.5 0 0 0 4 5.5v8A1.5 1.5 0 0 0 5.5 15H9"></path></svg><span class="sr-only" aria-live="polite"></span></button></span></div><div role="group" aria-label="text" class="docs-code-body"><pre class="shiki docs" tabindex="0"><code><span class="line">/compact            # summarize prior context to reclaim room</span>
<span class="line">/recap              # show a summary of recent activity</span>
<span class="line">/export transcript  # write the on-screen conversation to a .txt</span>
<span class="line">/export trajectory  # write the full session log to JSON</span>
<span class="line">/copy               # copy the last response to the clipboard</span></code></pre></div></div><ul class="docs-list"><li><span><strong><code class="docs-code-inline">/compact</code></strong> replaces earlier model-visible history with an LLM-generated summary to reclaim context room. It&#x27;s <strong>lossy</strong> for the model&#x27;s context (summarized, not verbatim), but does <strong>not</strong> clear your on-screen scrollback. Muse Code also compacts automatically when context fills. A manual <code class="docs-code-inline">/compact</code> never counts against the auto-compaction budget. Compaction fires the <a class="docs-link" href="/docs/muse-code/extending#hook-events"><code class="docs-code-inline">PreCompact</code> and <code class="docs-code-inline">PostCompact</code> hooks</a>.</span></li><li><span><strong><code class="docs-code-inline">/recap</code></strong> renders a short summary of what happened since the last recap, which is useful after you step away. It needs new activity to summarize, and runs between turns, not during one. Muse Code also shows a recap automatically when you come back after 2 minutes away, once the session has at least 2 of your messages. If a run is still going when you come back, the recap appears when that run finishes. A recap is a summary cell only. It doesn&#x27;t change the model&#x27;s context.</span></li><li><span><strong><code class="docs-code-inline">/export</code></strong> saves a session two ways: <code class="docs-code-inline">transcript</code> writes a human-readable <code class="docs-code-inline">conversation-&lt;stamp&gt;.txt</code> of the on-screen conversation, and <code class="docs-code-inline">trajectory</code> writes the full session log as JSON (the same document the <a class="docs-link" href="/docs/muse-code/extending#headless"><code class="docs-code-inline">muse export</code></a> CLI produces for the current session). Bare <code class="docs-code-inline">/export</code> opens a chooser. Add <code class="docs-code-inline">--out &lt;path&gt;</code> to pick a location and <code class="docs-code-inline">--redacted</code> to scrub secret-shaped strings.</span></li><li><span><strong><code class="docs-code-inline">/copy</code></strong> copies the markdown of the last completed response to your clipboard.</span></li></ul><h2 id="goals-loops" class="docs-h docs-h2">Goals and long-running loops<a class="docs-anchor" href="#goals-loops" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1">#</a></h2><p class="docs-p">For work that spans many turns, set a <strong>goal</strong>, and Muse Code holds the agent to it:</p><div class="docs-code"><div class="docs-code-head"><span class="docs-code-label">text</span><span class="docs-code-tools"><button type="button" class="docs-copy-btn" aria-label="Copy code" title="Copy code"><svg width="16" height="16" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.6" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" aria-hidden="true" focusable="false"><path d="M9 9h10.5v10.5H9z M15 9V5.5A1.5 1.5 0 0 0 13.5 4h-8A1.5 1.5 0 0 0 4 5.5v8A1.5 1.5 0 0 0 5.5 15H9"></path></svg><span class="sr-only" aria-live="polite"></span></button></span></div><div role="group" aria-label="text" class="docs-code-body"><pre class="shiki docs" tabindex="0"><code><span class="line">/goal &lt;objective&gt;       # set the session goal</span>
<span class="line">/goal                   # show the current goal</span>
<span class="line">/goal edit &lt;objective&gt;  # revise it</span>
<span class="line">/goal pause             # pause goal tracking</span>
<span class="line">/goal resume            # resume it</span>
<span class="line">/goal clear             # drop the goal</span></code></pre></div></div><p class="docs-p">With a goal set, the runtime keeps the agent working toward it. After a turn finishes, the runtime queues a follow-up to continue unfinished work, and it prompts the agent to <code class="docs-code-inline">report_progress</code> if the agent goes about 10 model steps without one. The goal reminder also holds the agent to a requirement-by-requirement completion check before it declares the goal done. When you interrupt a turn with <code class="docs-code-inline">Esc</code>, Muse Code automatically pauses an unfinished goal, and <code class="docs-code-inline">/goal resume</code> restarts it.</p><p class="docs-p">To run something on a schedule, use <strong><code class="docs-code-inline">/loop</code></strong>:</p><div class="docs-code"><div class="docs-code-head"><span class="docs-code-label">text</span><span class="docs-code-tools"><button type="button" class="docs-copy-btn" aria-label="Copy code" title="Copy code"><svg width="16" height="16" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.6" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" aria-hidden="true" focusable="false"><path d="M9 9h10.5v10.5H9z M15 9V5.5A1.5 1.5 0 0 0 13.5 4h-8A1.5 1.5 0 0 0 4 5.5v8A1.5 1.5 0 0 0 5.5 15H9"></path></svg><span class="sr-only" aria-live="polite"></span></button></span></div><div role="group" aria-label="text" class="docs-code-body"><pre class="shiki docs" tabindex="0"><code><span class="line">/loop 10m /run-tests          # every 10 minutes, run the /run-tests skill</span>
<span class="line">/loop "0 9 * * 1-5" standup   # weekdays at 9am (5-field cron)</span></code></pre></div></div><p class="docs-p"><code class="docs-code-inline">/loop</code> schedules a recurring prompt as a cron job. It accepts a shorthand interval (<code class="docs-code-inline">5m</code>, <code class="docs-code-inline">1h</code>, <code class="docs-code-inline">2d</code>) or a full 5-field cron expression (<code class="docs-code-inline">minute hour day-of-month month day-of-week</code>, local time). With no cadence, it defaults to every 10 minutes. The bundled command creates recurring jobs with <code class="docs-code-inline">fire_when_active_run: false</code>. An occurrence that lands during an active run is skipped, and the job remains scheduled for its next eligible occurrence. Skipped occurrences are not queued or replayed. Recurring jobs auto-expire after 7 days. A scheduled prompt can be a plain instruction or a <code class="docs-code-inline">/skill</code> invocation, and Muse Code passes it through verbatim.</p><div class="docs-callout docs-callout-note" role="note"><span class="docs-callout-icon"><svg width="20" height="20" viewBox="0 0 20 20" aria-hidden="true" focusable="false"><circle cx="10" cy="10" r="8.5" fill="currentColor"></circle><path fill="#fff" d="M9.1 8.6h1.8v5.6H9.1z M10 5.3a1.1 1.1 0 1 1 0 2.2 1.1 1.1 0 0 1 0-2.2z"></path></svg></span><div class="docs-callout-body"><p class="docs-callout-title">Loops use the cron tools</p><p class="docs-p">There is no dedicated loop-monitor panel. A loop is an ordinary scheduled job the agent manages with its cron tools. Pair it with a <code class="docs-code-inline">/goal</code> if you want the runtime to hold progress to a defined outcome.</p></div></div><h2 id="tasks" class="docs-h docs-h2">Track background tasks<a class="docs-anchor" href="#tasks" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1">#</a></h2><p class="docs-p">When the agent runs work in the background, such as long shell commands or monitors, you manage it through the Tasks surface:</p><div class="docs-code"><div class="docs-code-head"><span class="docs-code-label">text</span><span class="docs-code-tools"><button type="button" class="docs-copy-btn" aria-label="Copy code" title="Copy code"><svg width="16" height="16" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.6" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" aria-hidden="true" focusable="false"><path d="M9 9h10.5v10.5H9z M15 9V5.5A1.5 1.5 0 0 0 13.5 4h-8A1.5 1.5 0 0 0 4 5.5v8A1.5 1.5 0 0 0 5.5 15H9"></path></svg><span class="sr-only" aria-live="polite"></span></button></span></div><div role="group" aria-label="text" class="docs-code-body"><pre class="shiki docs" tabindex="0"><code><span class="line">/tasks      # open the Tasks drawer</span>
<span class="line">/subagents  # view running and past subagents</span>
<span class="line">/stop       # stop applicable background work</span></code></pre></div></div><ul class="docs-list"><li><span><strong><code class="docs-code-inline">/tasks</code></strong> opens a drawer for background tasks and direct subagents, with controls for the selected row.</span></li><li><span><strong><code class="docs-code-inline">/subagents</code></strong> opens the subagent view for running and completed descendants.</span></li></ul><h3 id="stop" class="docs-h docs-h3"><code class="docs-code-inline">/stop</code><a class="docs-anchor" href="#stop" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1">#</a></h3><p class="docs-p">Cancels applicable background tasks and terminals. It does not blanket-cancel direct subagents; manage those through <code class="docs-code-inline">/tasks</code>. This is different from <code class="docs-code-inline">Esc</code>, which only ends the current turn.</p><h2 id="workflows" class="docs-h docs-h2">Monitor workflows<a class="docs-anchor" href="#workflows" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1">#</a></h2><p class="docs-p">When workflows are available, run <code class="docs-code-inline">/workflows</code> to browse active and completed multi-agent workflow runs. The control room shows phases, child-agent progress, elapsed time, token usage, errors, and final results. You can pause, resume, cancel, skip, or restart a selected running child.</p><p class="docs-p">See <a class="docs-link" href="/docs/muse-code/workflows">run multi-agent workflows</a> for starting a workflow, writing reusable workflow scripts, and using the control-room keys.</p><h2 id="clarify" class="docs-h docs-h2">When the agent asks you a question<a class="docs-anchor" href="#clarify" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1">#</a></h2><p class="docs-p">Sometimes the agent needs a decision it can&#x27;t infer from the workspace. It pauses the turn and shows a short set of <strong>clarifying questions</strong>: one to three, each with a few options, single- or multi-select. Pick with the number keys, <code class="docs-code-inline">Space</code> toggles a multi-select option, <code class="docs-code-inline">Tab</code> adds an optional free-text note, <code class="docs-code-inline">←/→</code> moves between questions, and <code class="docs-code-inline">Enter</code> submits after a review step. <code class="docs-code-inline">Esc</code> interrupts instead of an answer.</p><p class="docs-p">Your answers are conversational input that steer the next steps. They don&#x27;t grant the agent any filesystem, shell, network, or approval authority. The agent asks only when the answer changes what it does next. It won&#x27;t stop to ask about things it can verify itself, or about conventional defaults.</p><p class="docs-p">To have the agent produce a plan and stop for your approval before it builds, invoke the built-in <code class="docs-code-inline">/plan</code> skill (see <a class="docs-link" href="/docs/muse-code/extending#skills">skills</a>).</p><h2 id="voice" class="docs-h docs-h2">Voice input<a class="docs-anchor" href="#voice" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1">#</a></h2><p class="docs-p">Dictate rather than type. Press <code class="docs-code-inline">Alt+V</code> (<code class="docs-code-inline">option-V</code> on macOS) to start or stop voice input. Muse Code transcribes your speech into the composer, and <code class="docs-code-inline">Enter</code> submits it like any other text.</p><div class="docs-code"><div class="docs-code-head"><span class="docs-code-label">text</span><span class="docs-code-tools"><button type="button" class="docs-copy-btn" aria-label="Copy code" title="Copy code"><svg width="16" height="16" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.6" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" aria-hidden="true" focusable="false"><path d="M9 9h10.5v10.5H9z M15 9V5.5A1.5 1.5 0 0 0 13.5 4h-8A1.5 1.5 0 0 0 4 5.5v8A1.5 1.5 0 0 0 5.5 15H9"></path></svg><span class="sr-only" aria-live="polite"></span></button></span></div><div role="group" aria-label="text" class="docs-code-body"><pre class="shiki docs" tabindex="0"><code><span class="line">/voice status   # show voice status</span>
<span class="line">/voice debug    # toggle voice diagnostics</span></code></pre></div></div><p class="docs-p">Voice is enabled by default on macOS, off by default on Linux, and unavailable on Windows. <code class="docs-code-inline">/voice</code> inspects state only. Turn voice on or off in <a class="docs-link" href="/docs/muse-code/configuration#settings-file"><code class="docs-code-inline">/settings</code></a>, not with <code class="docs-code-inline">/voice on</code>.</p><h2 id="images" class="docs-h docs-h2">Attach and reference images<a class="docs-anchor" href="#images" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1">#</a></h2><p class="docs-p">Paste or drop an image into the composer and Muse Code gives it an <code class="docs-code-inline">[Image #N]</code> label the model can see. Refer to an image by its number, such as &quot;what&#x27;s the error in <code class="docs-code-inline">[Image #2]</code>?&quot;, and the agent knows which one you mean. The labels and their source paths survive <a class="docs-link" href="/docs/muse-code/interactive#sessions">resume and fork</a>, and <a class="docs-link" href="/docs/muse-code/rewind">rewind</a>.</p><h2 id="reasoning" class="docs-h docs-h2">See the agent&#x27;s reasoning<a class="docs-anchor" href="#reasoning" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1">#</a></h2><p class="docs-p">While the agent works, Muse Code shows a live one-line <strong>reasoning summary</strong> in the status row (on by default). To commit the model&#x27;s full reasoning into your transcript, turn on <code class="docs-code-inline">show_reasoning</code> in <a class="docs-link" href="/docs/muse-code/configuration#settings-file">settings</a>. It&#x27;s off by default and independent of the summary line. <a class="docs-link" href="/docs/muse-code/configuration#reasoning-effort">Reasoning effort</a> governs how much reasoning the model produces (<code class="docs-code-inline">--reasoning-effort</code> or <code class="docs-code-inline">/effort</code>).</p><h2 id="session-model" class="docs-h docs-h2">How sessions work<a class="docs-anchor" href="#session-model" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1">#</a></h2><p class="docs-p">Muse Code records every run as an append-only event log: model calls, tool calls and their results, and approval decisions. Because the session is event-sourced, an interrupted or crashed run replays cleanly on <a class="docs-link" href="/docs/muse-code/interactive#sessions"><code class="docs-code-inline">/resume</code></a>. It rebuilds the conversation, closes the interrupted turn, and continues.</p><div class="docs-callout docs-callout-warning" role="note"><span class="docs-callout-icon"><svg width="20" height="20" viewBox="0 0 20 20" aria-hidden="true" focusable="false"><path fill="currentColor" d="M8.6 2.8a1.6 1.6 0 0 1 2.8 0l6.9 12a1.6 1.6 0 0 1-1.4 2.4H3.1a1.6 1.6 0 0 1-1.4-2.4l6.9-12z"></path><path fill="#fff" d="M9.1 6.8h1.8l-.2 5.2H9.3z M10 13.2a1 1 0 1 1 0 2 1 1 0 0 1 0-2z"></path></svg></span><div class="docs-callout-body"><p class="docs-callout-title">Verify resumed destructive steps</p><p class="docs-p">Treat a resumed destructive step as &quot;verify, then continue.&quot; Resume does <strong>not</strong> de-duplicate work that was in flight. Muse Code records a side effect interrupted mid-execution (for example a <code class="docs-code-inline">write_file</code> that partially landed) with an <strong>unknown</strong> outcome, and tells the agent to verify the actual state before it retries.</p></div></div><p class="docs-p">The same log powers <a class="docs-link" href="/docs/muse-code/interactive#context"><code class="docs-code-inline">/export trajectory</code></a> and post-hoc inspection with <code class="docs-code-inline">muse trace inspect</code>. Use <code class="docs-code-inline">muse --no-session-log</code> for an interactive session without a retained log, or <code class="docs-code-inline">muse exec --no-session-log</code> for a headless run. This forfeits resume, trajectory export and reattach, automatic retained-session naming and peer messaging, and retained workflow recovery (see <a class="docs-link" href="/docs/muse-code/extending#headless">headless and CI</a>).</p><h2 id="next-steps" class="docs-h docs-h2">Next steps<a class="docs-anchor" href="#next-steps" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1">#</a></h2><ul class="docs-list"><li><span>Set defaults, models, and project context in <a class="docs-link" href="/docs/muse-code/configuration">configuration and class="docs-prompt-preview" aria-label="Prompt preview" tabindex="0">You&#x27;re Claude Code, working in my repository.

Task
Make the page&#x27;s `/loop 10m /run-tests` example work in this repository: create a project skill at .agents/skills/run-tests/SKILL.md that runs this repo&#x27;s test command, summarizes failures in a few lines and changes nothing. Then add docs/muse-session.md for the team with the commands that matter here: /goal for long tasks, /loop with this skill, /compact and /recap, /fork and /rewind, /stop versus Esc, and the steering keys.

Read this first
Meta&#x27;s docs page &quot;Working with the agent&quot; as Markdown: https://dev.meta.ai/docs/muse-code/interactive.md
It&#x27;s the source of truth for request and response shapes. The same page for people: https://dev.meta.ai/docs/muse-code/interactive

Setup
- Muse Code: muse on PATH (install: curl -fsSL https://dev.meta.ai/install.sh | sh, or irm https://dev.meta.ai/install.ps1 | iex on Windows; check: muse --version). Its default model is muse-spark-1.2; --model picks another.
- Auth: muse reads META_API_KEY from the environment (in CI, from the secret store), else a key stored with muse auth set or a browser sign-in; not MODEL_API_KEY. Never hard-code, print or commit the key.
- Python: a plain script that runs muse through subprocess where a step needs it.

Facts to get right
- /loop takes an interval (5m, 1h, 2d) or a quoted 5-field cron in local time; no cadence means every 10 minutes. Jobs expire after 7 days; an occurrence during an active run is skipped.
- Project skills live at &lt;repo&gt;/.agents/skills/&lt;skill-id&gt;/SKILL.md (name and description front matter, as Claude Code and Codex skills use). Check one with `muse skills validate &lt;dir&gt;`.
- While a turn runs: Enter steers it, Alt+Enter queues for the next turn, Esc interrupts it (not background work: that&#x27;s /stop), Esc on an empty composer retracts the newest queued item.
- /compact summarizes context (lossy for the model; scrollback stays); /recap summarizes recent activity without changing context.
- /new keeps scrollback, /clear wipes it; /fork branches from the latest point; /rewind from an earlier message; /side opens a side conversation.

Starter code (Python)
import pathlib
import subprocess

skill = pathlib.Path(&quot;.agents/skills/run-tests/SKILL.md&quot;)
skill.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
skill.write_text(&quot;&quot;&quot;---
name: run-tests
description: Run this repo&#x27;s test suite and summarize failures. Used by /loop 10m /run-tests.
---
# Run the tests

1. Run the test command from the repo root (use this repo&#x27;s real one).
2. Report the pass and fail counts, then each failure in one line with its file.
3. Change nothing: no edits, no commits.
&quot;&quot;&quot;)
subprocess.run([&quot;muse&quot;, &quot;skills&quot;, &quot;validate&quot;, str(skill.parent)], check=True)

Done when
- `muse skills validate ./.agents/skills/run-tests` passes, and the skill uses this repo&#x27;s real test command.
- docs/muse-session.md lists /loop 10m /run-tests and each other command with one line on when to use it.
- The key comes from META_API_KEY or a stored sign-in and never appears in code, logs or commits.</pre><div class="docs-prompt-foot"><span class="docs-prompt-count">3,028<!-- --> characters</span><button type="button" class="docs-btn docs-btn-primary docs-btn-sm"><svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.6" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" aria-hidden="true" focusable="false"><path d="M9 9h10.5v10.5H9z M15 9V5.5A1.5 1.5 0 0 0 13.5 4h-8A1.5 1.5 0 0 0 4 5.5v8A1.5 1.5 0 0 0 5.5 15H9"></path></svg><span>Copy prompt</span></button></div></div></div><button type="button" class="docs-btn docs-btn-secondary" title="Copy this page as Markdown"><svg width="16" height="16" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.6" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" aria-hidden="true" focusable="false"><path d="M9 9h10.5v10.5H9z M15 9V5.5A1.5 1.5 0 0 0 13.5 4h-8A1.5 1.5 0 0 0 4 5.5v8A1.5 1.5 0 0 0 5.5 15H9"></path></svg><span>Copy page</span></button><a class="docs-btn docs-btn-secondary" href="https://dev.meta.ai/docs/muse-code/interactive" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer"><svg width="16" height="16" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.6" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" aria-hidden="true" focusable="false"><path d="M14 4h6v6 M20 4l-9 9 M18 14v4.5a1.5 1.5 0 0 1-1.5 1.5h-11A1.5 1.5 0 0 1 4 18.5v-11A1.5 1.5 0 0 1 5.5 6H10"></path></svg><span>View on dev.meta.ai</span><span class="sr-only"> (opens in a new tab)</span></a><p class="docs-rail-note">Independent concept built on Meta&#x27;s Model API.
